facts: Rachel Rudinger is affiliated with Johns Hopkins University.
Aaron Steven White is affiliated with the University of Rochester.
The research focuses on neural models of factuality.
The study aims to improve the factual accuracy of information in natural language processing tasks.
The study introduces two neural models for predicting event factuality.
The models demonstrate notable performance improvements on three datasets: FactBank, UW, and MEANTIME.
The authors expand the "It Happened" section of the Universal Decompositional Semantics dataset.
The extended dataset is the largest event factuality dataset to date.
The event factuality prediction task (EFP) involves labeling event-denoting phrases with their factuality status.
The authors present two neural models that significantly outperform previous systems on four existing datasets.
The extension of the UDS-IH1 dataset is named UDS-IH2.
UDS-IH2 encompasses the entire English Universal Dependencies v1.2 treebank.
Various syntactic categories can convey information about the factuality of events.
The verb "forget" demonstrates different effects of tensed and untensed predicates on factuality.
A study was conducted using two bidirectional LSTMs with different topologies.
The linear chain structure of the LSTM showed superior performance compared to previous models.
The FactBank corpus was developed by Saurí and Pustejovsky in 2009.
The UW dataset, created by Lee et al. in 2015, uses a crowdsourced scale from -3 to 3.
The UDS-IH1 dataset was annotated by White et al. in 2016.
Nairn et al. proposed rule-based methods for factuality prediction in 2006.
The UDS-IH2 dataset includes all predicates in EUD1.2.
A total of 32 annotators from Amazon Mechanical Turk annotated 20,580 predicates.
The inter-annotator agreement score for the HAPPENED question was 0.84.
UDS-IH2 exhibits a more entropic distribution of factuality ratings compared to other datasets.
The text discusses two neural models for predicting factuality.
One model is a stacked bidirectional linear chain LSTM.
The other model is a stacked bidirectional child-sum dependency tree LSTM.
A two-layer regression model uses the hidden state from the final layer of the stacked model at time t as input.
The model is a stacked bidirectional linear Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model.
The activation function for the cell state is the hyperbolic tangent (tanh).
The model incorporates multiple layers and bidirectional processing.
The Hadamard product is used in the calculations of the model.
The stacked bidirectional LSTM is referred to as stacked T-biLSTM.
The T-LSTM modifies the previous state to return indices of child nodes in a dependency tree.
The T-biLSTM does not incorporate dependency labels.
The model utilizes a ReLU pointwise nonlinearity.
The regression model predicts the factuality \( v_t \) of an event associated with a word \( w_t \).
The prediction \( \hat{v_t} \) is computed using the formula \( \hat{v_t} = V_2 g(V_1 h(L)_t + b_1) + b_2 \).
The model is evaluated using a smooth L1 loss function.
An ensemble method concatenates hidden states from both L-biLSTM and T-biLSTM.
The study implements L-biLSTM and T-biLSTM models using PyTorch 0.2.0.
The L-biLSTM utilizes a standard implementation, while the T-biLSTM employs a custom version available at decomp.net.
Both models use 300-dimensional GloVe 42B uncased word embeddings without tuning during training.
Evaluation metrics include mean absolute error (MAE) and Pearson correlation (r).
The L-biLSTM consistently outperforms the T-biLSTM.
The hybrid H-biLSTM excels in correlation on UW.
The addition of lexical features improves performance on UW.
Multi-task training is particularly beneficial for smaller datasets with closely related labels.
The analysis utilizes the UDS-IH2 dataset and gold dependency parses from EUD1.2.
Contexts without modals or negation exhibit the highest average factuality.
The presence of modals, particularly "will," correlates with lower factuality scores.
A manual error analysis of 50 events reveals that grammatical errors in UDS-IH2 significantly challenge model performance.
The study presents two advanced neural models for event factuality prediction: L-biLSTM and T-biLSTM.
The L-biLSTM generally demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional deterministic rule-based models.
The authors expanded the UDS-IH1 dataset to create UDS-IH2, the largest publicly available factuality dataset.
Experiments show that multi-task training across three unified factuality datasets leads to significant performance enhancements.
